I can deal with the Prowler later, and I only need to worry about Tempered Veteran if they get 6 mana (4WW to put the first counter).

Let me evaluate blocking:
- Patron of the Valiant: 4/4 FLYING - I can't block it with Markov Warlord (no flying). Takes 4 damage.
- Trusty Retriever: 4/5 - I can block with Markov Warlord (4/4). Warlord deals 4, Retriever survives at 4/1. Retriever deals 4, Warlord dies. Bad trade for me since Warlord is my only creature.

Wait - opponent has 3 untapped Plains + Tempered Veteran with vigilance. Veteran can tap with {W} to put a +1/+1 counter on Retriever (which has +1/+1 counters). So if I block Retriever, they can pump it to 5/6 and my Warlord still dies while Retriever survives at 5/2. 

If I don't block: I take 4+4 = 8 damage, going from 18 to 10. That's rough but I keep my Warlord.

If I block Retriever: I take 4 from Patron (18→14), but lose my Warlord to Retriever. And they still have everything.

I should not block. Taking 8 puts me to 10, but I keep Markov Warlord and can cast Scholar next main phase for a massive swing. Scholar + Meteor Golem from graveyard would be huge.

Turn 9! Drew Chromatic Sphere and Mudbutton Torchrunner. Opponent used Tempered Veteran on their turn to pump Trusty Retriever to 6/7 (4 counters)! That thing is massive. And they played an additional Plains (6 total).

My board is excellent though - Scholar 5/5 flying, Meteor Golem 3/3, Markov Warlord 4/4. All untapped and ready to attack. I have 8 untapped lands.

Let me plan:
- Hand: Bolt Hound (2R), Chromatic Sphere (1), Mudbutton Torchrunner (2R)
- I want to maximize damage this turn. Scholar flies over for 5 unblocked (no opposing flyers!). 

Opponent has Trusty Retriever 6/7 (untapped, can block) and Tempered Veteran 3/6 (tapped, can't block).

So if I attack with everything:
- Scholar 5/5 flying → unblocked → 5 damage
- Markov Warlord 4/4 → could be blocked by Retriever 6/7. Warlord dies, Retriever survives at 6/3. Bad.

annotations.description: Passed the turn with 2 untapped mana and Jousting Lance castable for {2}. No creatures on board yet, but deploying the equipment now costs nothing in tempo since the mana would go unused, and gets it ready for when Skyhunter Prowler arrives next turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, wasting 2 mana and ending the turn.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Jousting Lance for {2} to deploy it to the battlefield, so it's ready to equip once creatures are played in subsequent turns.

annotations.description: Fanatical Firebrand could attack for 1 unblocked damage against an empty board. Not attacking preserves the tap-sacrifice ping ability as a deterrent, but opponent only has 1 untapped Plains and limited options to play a relevant 1-toughness creature.
annotations.actionTaken: Did not attack with Fanatical Firebrand (timed out/no response)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Fanatical Firebrand for 1 free damage. The chance opponent plays a 1-toughness creature needing an immediate ping before your next untap is low with only 1 available Plains.

annotations.description: Fanatical Firebrand could attack for 1 unblocked damage since the opponent's only creature (Skyhunter Prowler) is summoning sick and can't block. There are no untapped creatures on the opponent's side at all. This is free damage with no downside - the Firebrand can still be sacrificed on the opponent's turn if needed.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not attack with Fanatical Firebrand.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Fanatical Firebrand for 1 unblocked damage.

annotations.description: Failed to block Fanatical Firebrand 1/1 with Skyhunter Prowler 1/3 (due to timeout). The Prowler would have killed the Firebrand for free while surviving, removing both a 1/1 attacker and its sacrifice-ping ability. Not blocking takes 1 unnecessary damage and leaves the Firebrand alive.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — did not block, took 1 combat damage from Fanatical Firebrand
annotations.betterLine: Block Fanatical Firebrand with Skyhunter Prowler. The Prowler survives (1/3 vs 1/1) and the Firebrand dies, removing a threat and its sacrifice ability.

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Skyhunter Prowler, a 1/3 flyer with vigilance, when the opponent has no flyers, no untapped creatures, and no untapped mana to interact. Attacking is completely free since vigilance means the creature stays untapped for blocking.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Skyhunter Prowler for 1 free damage. With vigilance, flying, and the opponent tapped out, there is zero risk.

annotations.description: Playing Mountain instead of Buried Ruin. Buried Ruin produces colorless mana (still counting toward generic costs for Markov Warlord) while also providing the powerful ability to recur Meteor Golem from the graveyard. There's no meaningful downside to playing Buried Ruin here since future land drops can be the Mountain or Island.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Mountain as their land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Buried Ruin to have access to its artifact recursion ability (targeting Meteor Golem in graveyard) while still producing mana toward future plays

annotations.description: Played Island instead of Buried Ruin. The only blue card in hand is nothing - the extra Island only helps with Aether Spellbomb's bounce mode (already have 1 Island for that). Buried Ruin produces colorless mana (equally useful for Markov Warlord's generic costs) while offering the powerful ability to return Meteor Golem from the graveyard to hand.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Island as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Buried Ruin to have the option of recovering Meteor Golem from the graveyard later, while still progressing toward casting Markov Warlord

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Skyhunter Prowler, a 1/3 flying vigilance creature, when the opponent has no flyers or reach. Vigilance means there's zero cost to attacking - the creature stays untapped for blocking. This is guaranteed free damage every turn.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Skyhunter Prowler for 1 unblockable damage. With vigilance, there is absolutely no downside to this attack.

annotations.description: Targeted Skyhunter Prowler instead of Tempered Veteran with Fiery Conclusion. Tempered Veteran is a +1/+1 counter engine that already has a counter on it, meaning it can activate for just {W} to put counters on itself or any other creature with a counter. Left alive, it will snowball the opponent's board. The Prowler is a threat but more static.
annotations.actionTaken: Targeted Skyhunter Prowler (2/4 flyer with vigilance) with Fiery Conclusion
annotations.betterLine: Target Tempered Veteran with Fiery Conclusion to shut down the counter engine. The Prowler can be bounced with Aether Spellbomb or blocked later by Scholar of the Lost Trove's 5/5 flying body.

annotations.description: Opus Sport passed with 3 untapped mana and no other plays available. Aether Spellbomb could have been sacrificed for {1} to draw a card, using otherwise-wasted mana. Alternatively, bouncing Tempered Veteran for {U} would remove its +1/+1 counter and delay the opponent's engine. Keeping the Spellbomb preserves optionality for future turns, but with Scholar of the Lost Trove planned for next turn (which could recast artifacts from graveyard), the value of holding it is reduced.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Aether Spellbomb, wasting 3 available mana.
annotations.betterLine: Sacrifice Aether Spellbomb for {1} to draw a card, or pay {U} to bounce Tempered Veteran and strip its +1/+1 counter. Drawing a card with unused mana is generally correct when no other plays exist.

annotations.description: Opus Sport passed with 3 untapped mana and no other plays available. They could have cycled Aether Spellbomb for {1} to draw a card, digging toward the lands needed for Markov Warlord (6 mana) or Scholar of the Lost Trove (7 mana). With Buried Ruin in hand able to recur the Spellbomb later if the bounce effect is needed, cycling now for card advantage with otherwise wasted mana is clearly better than doing nothing.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority, wasting 3 mana and ending the turn with no action taken.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb's {1} sacrifice ability to draw a card, using mana that would otherwise go to waste. Alternatively, pay {U} to bounce Tempered Veteran, removing its +1/+1 counter and forcing the opponent to replay it.

annotations.description: Markov Warlord has haste and 4 power, and the opponent's two creatures (Tempered Veteran and Trusty Retriever) were made unable to block by Markov Warlord's ETB trigger. Attacking is completely free 4 damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not attack with Markov Warlord, missing 4 free damage.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Markov Warlord for 4 unblockable damage, bringing the opponent from 19 to 15 life.

annotations.description: Casting Patron of the Valiant before playing Plains and activating Tempered Veteran's {W},{T} ability. By playing Plains first (6 lands), then activating Tempered Veteran ({W},{T}) to add a +1/+1 counter to a creature, then casting Patron (5 mana remaining), Patron's ETB would see more creatures with +1/+1 counters and distribute more counters. The current sequencing wastes the opportunity to get an extra +1/+1 counter from Tempered Veteran before Patron's ETB resolves.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Patron of the Valiant immediately, using all 5 available mana before playing the Plains in hand or activating Tempered Veteran.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, then activate Tempered Veteran ({W},{T}) to put a +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever (or itself), then cast Patron of the Valiant for {3}{W}{W} with the remaining 5 mana. Patron's ETB would then distribute more +1/+1 counters.

annotations.description: Markov Warlord's ETB ability makes up to two creatures unable to block this turn. With Patron of the Valiant being sick and the other two blockers (Tempered Veteran and Trusty Retriever) presumably targeted by the ETB, no creature can block. This is a free 4 damage to an opponent at 15 life. Even if ETB wasn't used optimally, attacking with a 4/4 haste creature that was cast specifically to pressure the opponent is critical, especially against a board that's growing with +1/+1 counters.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Markov Warlord.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Markov Warlord for 4 unblockable damage (assuming ETB targeted the two non-sick creatures), bringing opponent to 11 life and maintaining pressure.

annotations.description: Shining Armor has flash, so casting it in the precombat main phase wastes its surprise value. It could be held to use as a combat trick during blocks or on the opponent's turn to blank removal. Additionally, Bulwark Giant for 5 life and a 3/6 body might be the stronger play at 15 life against an aggressive red deck with Markov Warlord threatening damage.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Shining Armor in precombat main phase, giving away information before combat.
annotations.betterLine: Either hold Shining Armor (flash) and cast Jousting Lance + equip for an aggressive attack, or cast Bulwark Giant to gain 5 life and stabilize. Shining Armor should be kept in hand to use as a surprise during combat or on opponent's turn.

annotations.description: Failed to declare any attackers due to timeout. Patron of the Valiant is a 4/4 flyer that cannot be blocked by any creature on the opponent's board (Markov Warlord has no flying/reach). This is guaranteed 4 damage. Additionally, Tempered Veteran (3/6) and Trusty Retriever (4/5) could attack profitably since even if blocked by the 4/4 Markov Warlord, they survive combat. Missing a full attack step here wastes significant pressure.
annotations.actionTaken: No response (timeout) — no creatures attacked.
annotations.betterLine: At minimum attack with Patron of the Valiant for 4 unblockable flying damage. Ideally attack with all three creatures, as the ground creatures survive blocking from the 4/4 Markov Warlord and force unfavorable trades for the opponent.

annotations.description: Declined to activate Tempered Veteran's {W}, {T} ability during combat to put a +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever (which has +1/+1 counters and is attacking). This is a permanent upgrade for just 1 mana with no downside, and the player still had enough mana to cast Jousting Lance post-combat.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Tempered Veteran during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Tempered Veteran targeting Trusty Retriever to permanently make it 5/6 for {W}, then still have 3 mana available post-combat for Jousting Lance.

annotations.description: Tempered Veteran could activate its {W}, {T} ability to put a permanent +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever (or itself) during combat. This is free permanent value with no real downside - the Veteran isn't attacking, and with 4 untapped lands, spending 1W still leaves enough mana for post-combat plays like casting Jousting Lance (2 mana).
annotations.actionTaken: Passed without activating Tempered Veteran's ability during combat.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Tempered Veteran to put a +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever (making it 5/6), gaining permanent board value at minimal mana cost.

annotations.description: Passing on Tempered Veteran activation during combat. With 4 untapped lands and Tempered Veteran available, the player could put a +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever (or Tempered Veteran itself) for just {W}. If the opponent doesn't block, this is 1 extra damage (putting them to 1 instead of 2). The combat math against Markov Warlord blocking doesn't change, but the extra damage could matter when the opponent is at 10 life.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Tempered Veteran
annotations.betterLine: Activate Tempered Veteran to put a +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever before blocks, getting an extra point of damage through if unblocked, at minimal cost (1 white mana and tapping the Veteran which isn't attacking)

annotations.description: At 10 life facing 8 damage from Patron of the Valiant (4/4 flying) and Trusty Retriever (4/5), Opus Sport passed without activating Aether Spellbomb to bounce the Patron. By bouncing Patron and blocking Retriever with Markov Warlord, they could take 0 damage and stay at 10 life. Instead, they'll take at least 4 damage (blocking Retriever) or 8 (not blocking), dropping to dangerous life totals of 6 or 2.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Aether Spellbomb, taking full combat damage.
annotations.betterLine: Activate Aether Spellbomb paying {U} to bounce Patron of the Valiant, then block Trusty Retriever with Markov Warlord. This prevents all combat damage and keeps life total at 10, with Scholar of the Lost Trove castable next turn for a powerful recovery.

annotations.description: Passed on activating Tempered Veteran in response to Scholar of the Lost Trove's ETB (which is about to cast Meteor Golem from graveyard). The Meteor Golem will destroy a nonland permanent, potentially the Veteran itself, so getting value from the activation before it potentially dies seems prudent. The activation costs only {W} with 4 untapped lands available.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority without activating Tempered Veteran
annotations.betterLine: Activate Tempered Veteran ({W}, {T}) to put a +1/+1 counter on Trusty Retriever (or itself) before Meteor Golem potentially destroys the Veteran. This secures incremental value that could be lost entirely if Meteor Golem targets the Veteran.

annotations.description: Chose to destroy Patron of the Valiant (4/4 flyer) instead of Tempered Veteran (the counter engine). While Patron is a strong threat, Scholar of the Lost Trove (5/5 flyer) can block it after this turn. Tempered Veteran continuously grows the opponent's board each turn, making every creature increasingly difficult to deal with. The Veteran at 3/6 with 2 counters is also very resilient to removal.
annotations.actionTaken: Destroyed Patron of the Valiant with Meteor Golem's ETB
annotations.betterLine: Destroy Tempered Veteran to stop the counter engine, relying on Scholar of the Lost Trove to block Patron of the Valiant in subsequent turns

annotations.description: Opus Sport timed out and failed to attack with Markov Warlord into a completely tapped-out board. Both opposing creatures (Tempered Veteran and Trusty Retriever) are tapped, so the 4/4 Markov Warlord would deal 4 unblocked damage for free, bringing the opponent from 15 to 11. At 10 life themselves, applying pressure is critical.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out (no response), declaring no attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Markov Warlord for 4 unblocked damage, reducing opponent to 11 life.

annotations.description: Sacrificed Aether Spellbomb to draw a card when saving it for next turn's bounce mode ({U} activation) would have been significantly more valuable. The opponent has creatures with multiple +1/+1 counters (Trusty Retriever 5/6, Tempered Veteran 3/6) that are growing each turn via Tempered Veteran's ability. Bouncing one of these would remove all counters and tempo the opponent significantly. A random draw is much less impactful than a targeted bounce in this board state.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Aether Spellbomb's {1} draw mode, sacrificing it for a random card.
annotations.betterLine: Pass the turn and save Aether Spellbomb. Next turn with untapped Islands, use the {U} bounce mode to return the Trusty Retriever 5/6 (removing 3 +1/+1 counters) or another threatening creature, potentially enabling a lethal attack with the 5/5 flyer and other creatures.

annotations.description: Activating Tempered Veteran taps it, preventing it from attacking. With the opponent at 10 life and most of their board sick or tapped, maximizing combat damage this turn is critical. The +1/+1 counter doesn't compensate for losing 3 power in the attack.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tempered Veteran to place a +1/+1 counter, tapping it and removing it from the attack.
annotations.betterLine: Cast Jousting Lance (2 mana) and equip to Trusty Retriever (3 mana), giving it +2/+0 and first strike. Then attack with both Retriever (7/6 first strike) and Tempered Veteran (3/6) for 10 total power, potentially lethal or near-lethal depending on blocks.

annotations.description: Used Tempered Veteran's expensive ability ({4}{W}{W}) when the cheap ability ({W}) would have worked identically, since both creatures on board already have +1/+1 counters. This wasted 5 mana, preventing casting Bulwark Giant (which would have gained 5 life and provided a 3/6 blocker) while at 11 life facing Scholar of the Lost Trove 5/5 and Markov Warlord 4/4.
annotations.actionTaken: Activated Tempered Veteran's {4}{W}{W} ability to put a +1/+1 counter on a creature, spending 6 mana.
annotations.betterLine: Activate the {W} ability to put a +1/+1 counter on a creature that already has one (Trusty Retriever or Tempered Veteran), then cast Bulwark Giant for 6 mana to gain 5 life and add a 3/6 blocker.

annotations.description: Opus Sport had lethal on board and failed to attack (timeout). With Bolt Hound giving +1/+0 to other attackers, Scholar of the Lost Trove is a 6/5 unblockable flyer, and the opponent has only one untapped blocker (Trusty Retriever 6/7). Attacking with all creatures deals at minimum 12-13 damage against an opponent at 11 life — lethal regardless of how they block.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and declared no attackers, missing lethal.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures. Bolt Hound gives +1/+0 to others. Scholar (6 power, flying, unblockable) + two of {Markov Warlord 5/4, Meteor Golem 4/3, Bolt Hound 2/2} get through unblocked since opponent has only one ground blocker. Total unblocked damage exceeds 11 life — this is lethal.
